title: for over Lists
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to visit every item in a list with a for loop.
learn: for item in list visits each value
The loop variable holds the current item
You can print or use each item
idea: A for loop can walk through a list one item at a time: for name in team: Each time, name holds the current value. This is how you print every item without writing a separate line for each one.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change "Hello," to "Hi,". Press Run. Each greeting should start with Hi,.

practice.text: Loop over the fruit list and print each fruit on its own line.
practice.hint: Write for something in fruit: — pick any name for the loop variable, then indent a print line underneath.
practice.starterTip: For example: for f in fruit: then print(f) indented four spaces.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if a for loop prints each item in fruit.

practice.text: Print each number in nums with the word n: in front.
practice.hint: Inside print(), you can combine text and the variable with a comma, like print("n:", n).
practice.starterTip: Fill the empty print with something like print("n:", n) so each number gets a label.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if each number is printed with a label like n: 2.

quiz.question: What does for x in items: do?

options.text: Visits each item, setting x to the current value

quiz.correct: The loop variable gets each list value in order.
quiz.wrong: for walks through every item from start to end.

quiz.question: How many times does the loop body run for a 5-item list?
quiz.correct: Once per item — five items means five passes.
quiz.wrong: The body runs once for each item in the list.

quiz.question: In for name in team:, what is name?

options.text: The current item from the list

quiz.correct: name is the loop variable holding the current value.
quiz.wrong: Each pass, name is one item from team.
